paludohadros:study:1.title: A new iguanodontian dinosaur from the Weald Clay Formation (Lower Cretaceous) of Smokejacks Brickworks, southern England (Journal of Systematic Palaeontology, 2026)

facts.statement: Paludohadros lived during the Barremian stage of the Early Cretaceous in the United Kingdom’s Weald Clay Formation.
facts.quote: known from the Early Cretaceous (Barremian age) Weald Clay Formation of the United Kingdom

facts.statement: Paludohadros is a hadrosauroid ornithopod represented by a single species, P. proudlovii, known from a partial skull, skeleton, and isolated remains.
facts.quote: The genus contains a single species, Paludohadros proudlovii, known from a partial skull and skeleton, as well as various isolated remains.

facts.statement: Paludohadros is among several iguanodontian dinosaurs from the Weald Basin, but unlike others it comes from Barremian rocks rather than older Valanginian layers.
facts.quote: It is one of several iguanodontian dinosaurs known from the Weald Basin, though all others are from older Valanginian rock layers

facts.statement: The holotype consists of a partial skull, rib fragments, right pectoral girdle, forelimb elements, right ischium, hindlimb parts, and three tail vertebrae.
facts.quote: It consists of a partial skull (including several bones of the cranium, braincase, palate, and mandible) and various postcranial remains, including rib fragments, the right pectoral girdle, much of both forelimbs, the right ischium (a pelvic bone), parts of both hindlimbs, and three caudal (tail) vertebrae.

facts.statement: The generic name Paludohadros combines Latin 'palūs' (swamp) and Greek 'hadrós' (stout), referring to its swampy habitat and robust build.
facts.quote: The generic name, Paludohadros, combines the Latin word palūs, meaning swamp, with the Greek ἁδρός (hadrós), a suffix often used in hadrosauroid genus names meaning stout or robust.

facts.statement: The species name proudlovii honors William Proudlove, the manager of Smokejack Pit who died in 2000.
facts.quote: The specific name, proudlovii, honors William Proudlove, who managed the Smokejack Pit and died in 2000

facts.statement: The holotype individual of Paludohadros proudlovii is estimated to have been about 5 metres long.
facts.quote: The P. proudlovii holotype individual is estimated to have been about 5 m long.

facts.statement: The femur of the holotype measures 63 cm, intermediate in size between those of Mantellisaurus atherfieldensis and Comptonatus chasei.
facts.quote: The femur is 63 cm long, intermediate between the holotypes of Mantellisaurus atherfieldensis (57 cm) and Comptonatus chasei (73.5 cm)

facts.statement: Unfused vertebrae and a rugose texture on limb bones indicate the holotype was not fully mature at death.
facts.quote: The unfused vertebrae and rugose texture on the limb bones both suggest this individual was not fully mature when it died.

facts.statement: Distinctive anatomical features of Paludohadros include multiple ridges on lower jaw teeth, a dorsally projecting lateral process of the surangular, a proximal ridge on the humeral distal condyle, a posteroventrally curving ischium with a boot, and proximal tibial bosses.
facts.quote: The skeleton of Paludohadros is distinguished from other iguanodontians by several anatomical characters, including the number of ridges on the teeth of the lower jaw, the presence of a well developed dorsally (upward) projecting lateral process of the surangular bone of the lower jaw, the distal condyle of the humerus having a ridge that projects proximally (towards the body), the ischium curving posteroventrally (backwards and downwards) and has a well developed boot, and a tibia with bosses (growths) on the proximal end

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis places Paludohadros as the sister taxon to Istiorachis within an early-diverging hadrosauroid clade that also includes Xuwulong and Kukufeldia.
facts.quote: They recovered it as the sister taxon to Istiorachis, another Wealden taxon from the Wessex Formation. This clade of early-diverging hadrosauroids also included Xuwulong and Kukufeldia.

facts.statement: Paludohadros is the first dinosaur species named from the Barremian-aged Weald Clay of the Weald Basin.
facts.quote: Paludohadros is the first one named from the Weald Clay, as well as the first named based on fossils from Barremian-aged rocks in the Weald Basin.

facts.statement: The Weald Clay Formation, where Paludohadros was found, represents marshy, shallow floodplain environments with conifer forests and abundant ferns.
facts.quote: Analyses of the outcrops of the Weald Clay at Smokejack Clay Pit indicate that it was deposited in marshy conditions, the region being a shallow, temporary floodplain. Schizaceous ferns and tree ferns were the predominant undergrowth components within conifer forests.

facts.statement: Other dinosaurs from the same formation include the spinosaurid Baryonyx, the indeterminate maniraptoran Wyleyia, the ankylosaur Horshamosaurus, and the dryosaurid Valdosaurus.
facts.quote: In addition to Paludohadros, the spinosaurid theropod Baryonyx is also known from the Smokejack Clay Pit. Other localities have produced the indeterminate maniraptoran theropod Wyleyia, the ankylosaur Horshamosaurus, and the dryosaurid ornithopod Valdosaurus.
